environment: Two disposable Linux ARM64 Podman VMs, each 1 CPU and 2 GiB RAM, local XFS; stopped and removed

provider.observed: A second native process was refused while the holder lived; after SIGKILL and wait it acquired and released the same lock file.

group.observed: A legacy .epoch-lock directory refused without mutation. A concurrent process was refused while a test-instrumented holder was alive. Killing that holder after watermark publication released the flock automatically but the absent epoch stayed refused. Killing after initialized state released the flock automatically and a fresh process successfully prepared without manual unlock.

quorum.observed: Three authenticated native group servers with signed synthetic topology chose epochs 1 and 2. After SIGKILL of one server the others retained the first value. With one server down and a second epoch state removed, no majority was chosen and the missing file remained absent.

limits: Group owns its lock and writes within one process; do not generalize this to spawned child processes or a resource governor. The lock file must never be unlinked or replaced while any participant may run. Whole-directory rollback, sudden power loss, production keys, preexisting-state migration, Mac runtime, multi-host isolation, Tailscale transport, full bot and inference are not qualified.
